text:
emma_support: FYI customer (jane@acme) says GitHub/Google SSO intermittently fails with state_mismatch on redirect. Happens only when they use their custom domain through our edge proxy. They can reproduce ~60% of the time. Logs show initial /auth/start ok, then callback /auth/callback?state=... has a truncated state. Can someone triage?

samir_sre: thanks emma. do we have the full request examples from the browser and from our callback handler? need raw querystring and the state value we stored in session.

emma_support: pasted the snippets they sent. note the state we stored (SHA256 hex) is 64 chars; callback sometimes shows ~40 chars and then an extra queryparam appended.

allan_engineer: hmm maybe the edge worker or their CDN is rewriting long querystrings or cutting at a comma/semicolon. can you paste the exact redirect the browser follows?

emma_support: browser redirect (from google):
```
GET https://login.acme.example.com/auth/callback?state=7f3b2e9c5a1f4b6d8e2c9a0f4b6d8e2c9a0f4b6d8e2c9a0f&session=eyJhbGciOiJI...
```
But our server received:
```
GET /auth/callback?state=7f3b2e9c5a1f4b6d8e2c9a0f4b6d8e2c9&session=eyJhbGciOiJI...
```
(the tail of the state missing)

samir_sre: looks like truncation is happening before it hits our origin. could be our edge worker URL normalize code or their CDN dropping after some character. do we run any querystring canonicalization for custom domains? allan?

allan_engineer: we do have a small module in edge that canonicalizes params: it collapses duplicate keys and enforces max param length of 48 char by default (old guardrail). that would explain a 64->48 cut. i thought it applied only to internal routes but maybe we accidentally applied it on proxy passthrough for customer custom domains.

emma_support: oh wow. customer state is generated by the browser oauth library (pkce lib) and length varies. when it's cut we get mismatch -> state_mismatch. any chance to bump that cap quickly?

allan_engineer: can push a hotfix to config to disable truncation for /auth/* on custom domains. patch looks like (edge worker pseudo):
```
- if (param.length > 48) param = param.slice(0,48)
+ if (route.startsWith('/auth/')) return param // do not truncate
```
I want to run it by infra first.

devops-bot: deploy queued: edge-worker-config -> canary to us-east in 10m if approved.

samir_sre: quick mitigations we can offer customer: 1) advise using base64url state shorter than 48 chars, 2) temporary workaround: append state in fragment (#) and exchange via PRG, but that's messy. better to change our edge behavior.

emma_support: customer tried rolling back their CloudFront worker and problem goes away 100% — they confirmed. sounds like CF worker changed querystring behavior. but they still want us to support arbitrary state lengths.

allan_engineer: ok i'll put up the config change and a small test to ensure we don't accidentally expose long param attacks. security: do we have an upper bound we can validate server-side? we should still validate state length < 1024 or something.

samir_sre: agree. server-side should reject absurdly long states but allow up to 512 by default. also add logging to capture both stored_state and incoming_state length to help future triage.

emma_support: i'll communicate interim workaround to customer and let them know we have a canary deploy scheduled. can you confirm the deploy window?

devops-bot: deploy started: edge-worker-config canary -> us-east. changelist: skip-truncate-auth-params, add-param-length-logging.

allan_engineer: canary looks good in us-east after running auth flow 50x. no truncation, logs show state length preserved. rolling to global in 15m.

samir_sre: after global rollout, run a smoke script that hits /auth/start -> external provider -> callback and verify state matches stored value for at least 200 samples. also monitor support for repeats.

emma_support: customer confirmed tests passing post-rollout. they said it was intermittent before and now login succeeds. they're happy for now but asked what caused it — they run a custom CloudFront worker that normalizes querystrings; that combined with our old 48-char guard resulted in truncation.

allan_engineer: filing a small postmortem note: root cause = overly aggressive param-length guard enabled in edge canonicalizer applied to customer-facing custom domains. fix = exempt auth routes and add server-side validation to accept larger states. followups: update docs recommending state < 512, add telemetry for truncated params.

emma_support: thanks team. I'll mark the ticket resolved and send the customer a short summary + our recommended best-practices. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround! :heart:
